options.why: Subtracted $180^{\circ}$ (a straight angle) instead of a full $360^{\circ}$ revolution.
Subtracted $340^{\circ}$ instead of $360^{\circ}$, an arithmetic slip on the turn size.
Measured the leftover $80^{\circ}$ back from $360^{\circ}$ instead of taking it as the answer.

questions.question_text: Which of these angles is equivalent (coterminal) with $70^{\circ}$?

options.why: This is $360^{\circ}-70^{\circ}$, a reflection across the $x$-axis, not a whole-turn equivalent.
This is the supplement $180^{\circ}-70^{\circ}$, which points in a different direction.
This is the opposite rotation, which lands at $290^{\circ}$, not at $70^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
Add a full turn of $360^{\circ}$ to keep the same direction.
$70^{\circ}+360^{\circ}$
$\equiv 430^{\circ}$
So $430^{\circ}$ is coterminal with $70^{\circ}$.
